title: As Mossad chief visits US, fears grow Netanyahu could strike Iran to block Eisenkot
gist: Israeli opposition leaders fear caretaker PM Netanyahu could provoke a renewed Iran confrontation during the 42-day transition to block a government led by Gadi Eisenkot, who has 67 Knesset recommendations, as Mossad chief Roman Gofman lobbies Washington to resume strikes.

insights.claim: Israeli opposition leaders fear Netanyahu could provoke Iran into reigniting military confrontation to prevent a new government under rival Gadi Eisenkot.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Israeli domestic politics is a live trigger for renewed Iran war during the transition window.
insights.locator: TEL AVIV — Israeli opposition leaders fear

insights.claim: Eisenkot received recommendations from 67 Knesset members versus 46 for Netanyahu and was tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming a government, though coalition talks are difficult.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Leadership change in Israel is likely but not locked; coalition failure risk persists.
insights.locator: Eisenkot received the recommendations of 67 Knesset members

insights.claim: During the 42-day transition period Netanyahu remains in power as caretaker prime minister.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Defines the time window of elevated escalation risk.

insights.claim: Per Axios, Mossad Director Roman Gofman is in Washington, met CIA Director John Ratcliffe, is expected to meet Marco Rubio and may meet Steve Witkoff, as part of Netanyahu's push for Trump to resume military operations against Iran.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Israeli lobbying raises the probability of renewed US strikes on Iran.
insights.locator: Citing three sources familiar with the matter

insights.claim: Political uncertainty in Israel and Trump's continued zigzagging on Iran are adding to tensions among Israelis exhausted by three years of war and inconclusive Oct. 27 elections.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: US policy inconsistency amplifies regional uncertainty.
